subject.title: [Bug]: Potential resource leak in runBoundTurnWithMissingThreadRecovery -- retry not wrapped in try/finally after thread spawn

question: Should Codex app-server conversation bindings keep a persistent subscription between bound turns, or should each bound turn explicitly reattach and then unsubscribe in cleanup?
rationale: Both choices can be valid, but the code change is unsafe without maintainer intent because naive unsubscribe fixes the reported leak while risking follow-up message delivery for saved bound threads.

options.title: Per-turn reattach and cleanup
options.body: Before each bound turn, explicitly ensure the app-server connection is subscribed to the saved thread, then best-effort unsubscribe in finally so retry failures cannot strand subscriptions.

options.title: Persistent binding subscription
options.body: Treat the subscription as part of the active conversation binding lifecycle, document that the replacement thread remains subscribed, and close or narrow this report to detach/unbind cleanup only.

options.title: Target only failed replacement threads
options.body: Clean up only replacement-thread retry failures and add a follow-up guard so the next bound turn can reattach or fail with a clear recovery path.

recommendation.title: Per-turn reattach and cleanup
recommendation.body: Before each bound turn, explicitly ensure the app-server connection is subscribed to the saved thread, then best-effort unsubscribe in finally so retry failures cannot strand subscriptions.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete committed the recovery behavior and has adjacent Codex app-server lifecycle history in the affected paths.
